risks.title: Critical dependence on licensing partners
risks.summary: Biodexa is entirely reliant on external partners for regulatory approval and commercialization of its drug candidates (eRapa, tolimidone). The absence of a viable partner or failure of commercial negotiations could halt development and prevent any revenue generation (royalties, milestones).
risks.score_rationale: Risk placed at the beginning of the Risk Factors section with very direct language ("Our future success is dependent"). High intensity: business model entirely based on ability to secure partners for development and commercialization. Stable but structural trend. Major weight category for early-stage biotech.

risks.title: Risk of clinical trial failure and regulatory approval
risks.summary: All of Biodexa's drug candidates (eRapa, tolimidone) are in clinical or preclinical development. Preclinical study results do not predict subsequent clinical outcomes. Obtaining regulatory approvals from the FDA, EMA, and MHRA is lengthy, unpredictable, and not guaranteed.
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned 4 times in the Risk Factors section with maximum intensity language ("substantially harmed", "inherently unpredictable"). All candidates are in clinical/preclinical phase. FDA/EMA processes described as "lengthy, time consuming and inherently unpredictable". Critical weight for biotech.

risks.title: Dependence on third-party manufacturers and suppliers
risks.summary: Biodexa relies entirely on third parties for clinical and commercial manufacturing of its drug candidates. Any quality failure, delivery delay, regulatory non-compliance, or supplier price increase could stop or delay development and reduce future profitability.
risks.score_rationale: Two distinct risks mentioned: reliance on third-party manufacturers for clinical trials and commercial supply, and dependence on third-party suppliers. Moderate-to-high intensity language ("could be stopped, delayed or made less profitable"). Stable trend. Significant weight for biotech without internal manufacturing capabilities.

risks.title: Absence of recurring revenue and unproven business model
risks.summary: Biodexa has generated only minimal revenue to date and has no sources of recurring revenue. The model relies on securing licensing partners and achieving milestones/royalties, which are not expected in the near term. No guarantee of future profitability even if regulatory approval is obtained.
risks.score_rationale: Fundamental risk repeated 3 times ("no sources of recurring revenue", "minimal amount of revenue"). Very direct language on commercial uncertainty. Stable but structural trend. Critical weight: no candidate has generated revenue to date.

risks.title: Risk of loss of key and scientific personnel
risks.summary: Biodexa operates with limited resources and may face difficulties in recruiting and retaining qualified scientists, key executives, and consultants. Loss of key personnel could delay development efforts and impair the ability to advance drug candidates.
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned in Risk Factors ("unable to retain and recruit qualified scientists, key executives"). Moderate language ("may delay our development efforts"). Stable trend. Moderate weight for early-stage biotech with limited resources.

risks.title: Inadequate protection of intellectual property
risks.summary: Biodexa's success depends on its ability to obtain and maintain patent protection for its drug candidates and proprietary technology. Lack of adequate IP protection or patent expiration could allow competitors to copy or circumvent the technology.
risks.score_rationale: Explicit risk: "Our success depends in part on our ability to protect rights in our intellectual property, which cannot be assured". Direct uncertainty language ("cannot be assured"). Stable trend. Significant weight for biotech whose value relies on patents and proprietary technology.

risks.title: Intense competition in the pharmaceutical/biotech industry
risks.summary: The pharmaceutical and biotechnology industries are highly competitive. The commercial success of any Biodexa drug candidate depends on market acceptance against existing or future competing therapies, including alternative treatments for the same indications.
risks.score_rationale: Explicit risk: "The pharmaceutical and biotechnology industries are highly competitive". Direct but generic language. Stable trend. Moderate-to-significant weight: competition affects commercial adoption and candidate viability.

risks.title: Geopolitical risk related to Brexit and UK/EU regulation
risks.summary: Biodexa is exposed to political, regulatory, and economic risks related to the United Kingdom's exit from the European Union. Changes in UK, EU, and US regulatory regimes, as well as difficulties conducting international business, could affect regulatory approval and commercialization of drug candidates.
risks.score_rationale: Explicit risk mentioned twice: "exposed to political, regulatory, social and economic risk relating to the United Kingdom's exit from the European Union". Moderate language. Stable trend but post-Brexit context. Moderate weight for UK-based biotech with access to EU/US markets.
